flashcard_questions.q: Where in the body is urea produced?
flashcard_questions.a: In the liver, when excess amino acids are broken down.

flashcard_questions.q: What is ultrafiltration in the glomerulus?
flashcard_questions.a: High blood pressure forces water, glucose, urea and ions out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule.

flashcard_questions.q: How much of the filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules?
flashcard_questions.a: All of it, by active transport.

flashcard_questions.q: Which substance in the filtrate is not reabsorbed at all?
Which gland releases ADH into the blood?
Which part of the brain detects that the blood has become too concentrated?
What effect does more ADH have on the kidney tubules?
flashcard_questions.a: They become more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed.

flashcard_questions.q: What sort of urine is produced when little ADH is released?
flashcard_questions.a: A large volume of dilute urine.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does dialysis fluid hold the same glucose concentration as normal blood?
flashcard_questions.a: There is then no concentration gradient, so glucose is not taken out of the blood.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must a kidney transplant patient take immunosuppressant drugs for life?
flashcard_questions.a: To stop the immune system attacking and rejecting the donated kidney.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does auxin have on cell elongation in a shoot?
flashcard_questions.a: It promotes elongation, so more auxin means more growth.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does auxin have on cell elongation in a root?
flashcard_questions.a: It inhibits elongation, so more auxin means less growth.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a shoot bend towards a light source?
flashcard_questions.a: Auxin moves to the shaded side, where the cells then elongate more.

flashcard_questions.q: Which plant hormone is used commercially to ripen fruit?
In the cress phototropism practical, what is the independent variable?
